references.text: Jethro advised Moses to select capable men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain, to serve as leaders over the people - the same principle of choosing qualified leaders.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them as rulers over the people - a parallel account of appointing leaders.
The Lord commanded Moses to gather seventy men from the elders of Israel whom he knew were elders and overseers of the people - a similar selection of recognized leaders.
Proverbs highlights wisdom as a virtue that leaders should seek - corresponding with the requirement for wise men.
The apostles asked the congregation to choose seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom - a New Testament parallel to choosing recognized and wise men for leadership.
Paul lists qualifications for overseers who must have a good testimony and be temperate - corresponding requirements for recognized and prudent leaders.
Paul instructs Titus to appoint elders in every city with specific qualifications - a New Testament application of the principle of appointing qualified leaders.
